sections.h2: What the Delaware County recorder does for a home seller
sections.html:
The recorder's office indexes all real estate and personal property records for Delaware County, collects the filing fees, and keeps military service discharge records. When a house sells, two papers land on its desk: the deed that gives the buyer title, and the satisfaction that shows the seller's lender has been paid.

Visit 145 N. Union St., Delaware, OH 43015, or call (740) 833-2460. Recordings are accepted on weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30, holidays excluded. The cutoff for submitting documents is 4:00 p.m., and an exam room is open to the public during the same hours. The recorder's site also offers a recorded document search, a military graves search and a property fraud page.

sections.h2: What does filing a two-page deed cost in Delaware County?
sections.html:
The fee page lists $39.00 for the first two pages of a deed, mortgage, lease, power of attorney, release or assignment on paper 8.5 by 14 inches or smaller, and $8.00 for every page after that. A footnote explains that the $39.00 already contains the $5.00 preservation surcharge permitted by ORC 317.32.

Document or serviceCharge
Basic instrument, first 2 pages$39.00, then $8.00 per added page
Marginal reference on a release, amendment or assignment$4.00 each
Map, plat or print, recorded or certified$40.00 per page
Federal tax lien: original or release$5.00 or $3.00
Living will or health care power of attorney$40.00 flat per document
Photocopy, and certified copy$2.00 per page, and $2.00 per page plus $2.00 to certify
Veteran's dischargeNo fee

Behind these numbers is ORC 317.32, which splits the first-two-pages price into a $17 base fee and a $17 housing trust fund fee. Each added page carries $4 plus $4, and a county may add a preservation surcharge of up to $5. If you mail a document, enclose a postage-paid return envelope or enough cash to cover the postage.

sections.h2: The auditor comes before the recorder
sections.html:
When a county levies a real property transfer tax, ORC 322.02 makes the grantor named in the deed pay it to the county auditor at delivery of the deed, ahead of presenting the deed to the recorder. The buyer also files a statement of value with the auditor under ORC 319.202 before the deed is endorsed.

State law caps a county's transfer tax at thirty cents per hundred dollars of value. Because the commissioners set the rate by resolution, call the auditor at (740) 833-2900 close to the closing date to learn the one in force.

  • Auditor first: value statement, any transfer tax, and the endorsement on the deed.
  • Recorder second: the endorsed deed, the page-count fee, and a return envelope if the package is mailed.
  • Same building: both offices share 145 N. Union St., so a hand delivery needs only one trip.
  • Last stop: the online document search, to see that the deed shows against the right parcel.

The fee schedule reads like a map of what can cloud or clear a title. Federal tax liens cost $5.00 to record in original, corrected, refiled, partial release or subordination form, and a release costs $3.00. Uniform Commercial Code filings such as fixture filings and continuation statements cost $12.00 plus $4.00 for each name indexed, and a UCC search costs $20.00.

Other entries a homeowner may meet include zoning resolutions at a $50.00 flat fee, zoning amendments at $20.00, attested accounts that place liens on public funds, a motor vehicle bond lien at $10.00, and Bureau of Workers' Compensation releases, which are free. A bill of sale in a bulk sale carries no fee either.

Ask the title company which of these appear against your name before you list. A federal tax lien or a stale mortgage that was never released can slow down a buyer's lender, and the recorder's online search shows what is on file.

The recorder's Real Estate Recording page borrows definitions from a real estate dictionary. A general warranty deed is one where the grantor agrees to protect the grantee against any other claim to title and adds further promises. A special warranty deed narrows that promise to anyone claiming by, from, through or under the grantor, with no warranty against title defects from before the grantor owned the land.

A quitclaim deed passes along only whatever rights the grantor has, without naming those rights and without warranties of ownership. Recording means entering an instrument in the public books, which gives notice to the world. The sale contract and the title agent decide which deed form a sale uses. The recorder's office does not pick it.

sections.h2: Where Delaware County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
Every parcel in the county records here, whichever town it sits in. The city of Delaware is the seat, and Powell, Sunbury and the Delaware County portions of Dublin and Westerville are also inside the county, along with the villages of Ashley, Galena, Ostrander and Shawnee Hills.

  • A deed for a Powell, Sunbury or Delaware house goes to the same recorder as one for a township farm.
  • Dublin and Westerville lie partly in other counties, so a mailing address in either one does not tell you which recorder applies. Check the parcel record first.
  • The auditor's GIS property search shows which parcel number to cite on the paperwork.

The deed is only the last step. Before it is filed, confirm that your old mortgage has a recorded satisfaction, since a lender's release is a separate paper from the deed. Gather the parcel number from the auditor's GIS search, ask the auditor what transfer tax applies, and decide who will carry the package. A title company usually handles all of this for a sale.

Cash sales skip the buyer's lender, but the deed still goes through the auditor and then the recorder, and the same fee schedule applies. When the package is accepted, use the online document search to confirm the deed appears against the right parcel, and keep a copy for your own files. If something looks wrong, such as a wrong parcel or a misspelled name, call the recorder at (740) 833-2460 before the closing date passes, because fixing an error later can mean a second filing and a second set of fees.

Households here have high ownership costs: median monthly owner costs are $2,493 with a mortgage and $986 without, and median gross rent is $1,492. Population grew from 174,214 in 2010 to 214,124 in 2020 and is estimated at 242,032 for 2025.

faqs.q: What is the Delaware County recording fee for a three-page deed?
faqs.a: The schedule posts $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page after that, so the third page is billed at the $8.00 rate. Marginal references on releases and assignments cost $4.00 each and are billed separately.

faqs.q: When must a document reach the Delaware County recorder?
faqs.a: The submission cutoff is 4:00 p.m., while the office itself works from 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays. Holidays are excluded.

faqs.q: Does the Delaware County recorder charge for a veteran's discharge?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule marks a veteran's discharge, and an expunged discharge, as no fee.

faqs.q: Who pays Delaware County's transfer tax at closing?
faqs.a: State law puts it on the grantor, meaning the seller named in the deed, and it goes to the auditor before recording. Ask the auditor's office at (740) 833-2900 what rate applies.

faqs.q: Can I look up Delaware County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Yes. The recorder's home page links a recorded document search. Use it to check that your deed or a mortgage release was recorded.
